chapter: Ben Pollack band and New York
title: After Pollack: Goodman to Paramount, McPartland to 'Sons of Guns'
summary: The band thinks of rehearsing 'Pollack's band without Pollack', but Goodman gets a job with Rubinoff and McPartland one in the Broadway show.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: Oh, he didn't take it back?

No, he didn't. The manager wanted him to be a real hard, down to earth leader style you know. And so all the guys got down on him. Everybody was mad at him. Jack T, everybody, the whole band. And we were going to, what we were going to do was, actually we all got together and had a big meeting and we started to rehearse on our own without Pollack. We were going to call it Pollack's band without Pollack. (LAUGHTER).

So we started to go like that. We were going to do that. However, I happened to hear of a job at the Paramount Theater that they needed a saxophone clarinet player and I called up Benny right away and told him I heard that they needed... Rubinoff the violin player.

Rubinoff needed a clarinet player, a saxophone player and I called, well I was living, Benny and I were living together what am I talking about. So I told Benny about it and he went over and he got the job. And the same thing happened with me. Mannie Klein the trumpet player was talking to Benny Goodman about he didn't want to take a job with a show called, 'Sons of Guns'. Jack Donahue and Lily Damita (Louis Damita?) on Broadway.

So, Benny Goodman said, well get Jimmy McPartland. He plays second trumpet and plays jazz, hot, you know, they call it hot cornet you know, hot. Playing hot in those days we would call it. Can you play hot? You know, jazz. Hot jazz. So I went over and auditioned for the job and I got the job in 'Sons of Guns'.
